Oster Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Oster's Jews, present from the 18th century, grew to 1,596 (29 percent) by 1897, supporting four synagogues by 1886. The community survived pogroms in 1905 and 1919-1920, though many left for larger cities afterward. On October 29, 1941, a Sonderkommando 4A detachment shot 215 Jews and other locals; 279 Jews in total were shot between 1941 and 1943. In March 1946, the remains of Holocaust victims were reinterred in a mass grave at this cemetery, which itself lost its longtime groundskeeper in February 2020, leaving it unprotected since.
